title: Decide Larastan max-violation gate policy (carve-outs vs baseline vs fix-in-place)
description:
## What

Decide how the project gates PRs given that phpstan level: max now reports 143 violations in unchanged starter-kit code (was 0 at #18 resolution time — see discovery in bd samples-20260717-1784648472636-14-eac5a270.1 notes).

 ## Why this exists

bd samples-20260717-1784648472636-14-eac5a270.1 (the 'edit phpstan.neon to level: max' bead) cannot be closed because composer types:check exits 1 with 143 violations. The 143 break down:
- 61 staticMethod.dynamicCall (strict-rules; stylistic — mostly Assert:: and Eloquent Builder:: calls in tests)
- 36 property.nonObject + method.nonObject (real nullable safety — mostly Auth::user() returning User|null in tests/middleware)
- 17 booleanNot/if.condNotBoolean/elseif.condNotBoolean/booleanAnd.leftNotBoolean (strict-rules)
-  7 typeCoverage.paramTypeCoverage (peststan — 94.5% < 99%)
- 22 misc (argument.type, return.type, arrayFilter.strict, empty.notAllowed, singletons)

#17 already adopted 'strict from day 0 with shrinking ignoreErrors carve-outs, no global baseline file' as the policy shape for arch() rules. #18's resolution reaffirmed 'level: max + no baseline' for Larastan. So a generated baseline (option 1) is FORBIDDEN by existing policy.

 ## Decision required

Choose one (or hybrid):
1. FORBIDDEN: --generate-baseline + phpstan-baseline.neon (violates #17 precedent).
2. PREFERRED PER POLICY: scoped ignoreErrors in phpstan.neon for specific strict-rules identifiers (e.g. staticMethod.dynamicCall) that are stylistic, each linked to a follow-up execution ticket that fixes the underlying code. Real nullable violations get fixed, not ignored.
3. FIX NOW: address all 143 violations in code before any further feature work. Mostly starter-kit code (Teams/Fortify) that Filament 5 / Spatie Permission will likely reshape anyway.
4. LOWER LEVEL: gate at level 0 (still 47 violations — same problem smaller). Not viable long-term.

 ## Source decision

Supersedes/refines #18 (bd-17). Should be resolved BEFORE the Filament 5 install sequence (#16 step 1) so all new Filament code is held to a known policy from its first commit. Currently blocks bd samples-20260717-1784648472636-14-eac5a270.1 and any subsequent PR that touches types:check.
notes:
## Resolution (2026-07-22)

### Decision: Hybrid — keep strict-rules, one permanent carve-out, fix everything else in code

**Policy stance:** Keep all strict-rules packages (operator's deliberate choice in a91c5b0). #18's policy (level: max, no baseline) stands. #18's "0 violations" factual premise is corrected: it was true before a91c5b0 added strict-rules companion packages, false after. The 143 violations are the TRUE state of the starter kit at level: max with strict-rules + peststan + type-coverage installed.

### 1. Permanent carve-out: staticMethod.dynamicCall (61 violations)

The sole strict-rules identifier structurally incompatible with Eloquent's query builder API. All 61 instances are canonical Laravel calls (Model::where(), $relation->exists(), etc.). No amount of code changes fixes this without abandoning the query builder.

**Policy refinement to #17:** permanent framework-idiom carve-outs are exempt from the retiring-ticket citation requirement. They carry a `# framework-idiom: <justification>` comment instead, reviewed when the framework or PHPStan major version changes. This does not weaken the shrinking-carve-outs principle — it recognizes that framework incompatibilities are not debts to retire, they are permanent boundaries.

### 2. Fix all 82 remaining violations in code — zero additional carve-outs

| Category | Count | Fix approach | Bead |
|----------|-------|-------------|------|
| Nullable-safety (tests) | 35 | assert(auth()->check()) guards — narrows type for PHPStan, preserves loud-failure | .3 |
| Nullable-safety (app) | 1 | Null check | .3 |
| Strict-rules boolean strictness | 17 | ! \$x → \$x === null, explicit boolean conditions | .4 (new) |
| Strict-rules misc (empty, ternary, function.strict, arrayFilter) | 7 | Idiomatic rewrites | .4 |
| Peststan param type coverage | 7 | Add missing param type declarations | .4 |
| Core PHPStan type issues | 15 | Individual fixes (argument.type, return.type, method.childParameterType, etc.) | .4 |

### 3. Nullable-safety fix approach: assert guards (not nullsafe operators)

In tests, Auth::user() is guaranteed non-null by Auth::login() in setup, but PHPStan can't track that. Using nullsafe operators (?->) would silently return null on unexpected failures (confusing assertion failures). Using assert(auth()->check()) narrows the type for PHPStan while preserving loud TypeError behavior if assumptions break. Applied to 35 test sites.

### 4. Bead restructuring

- .3 stays scoped to nullable-safety (36 violations) — approach changes to assert guards.
- New .4 covers the remaining 46 fixes (24 strict-rules style + 7 peststan + 15 misc).
- Both unblock when .2 closes. .1 closes when .3 + .4 land and types:check exits 0.

### 5. Gate policy (terminal state)

phpstan.neon: level: max, tests/ in paths, one ignoreErrors entry (staticMethod.dynamicCall, permanent framework-idiom, # framework-idiom: Eloquent query builder uses dynamic calls to static methods by design).

Verification command: XDEBUG_MODE=off php -d xdebug.mode=off vendor/phpstan/phpstan/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M --no-progress — exits 0 with the carve-out + all code fixes.

### Violation inventory (143 total, fully categorized)

By source package:
- phpstan-strict-rules: 85 (staticMethod.dynamicCall 61 + booleanNot.exprNotBoolean 13 + if/elseif.condNotBoolean 3 + booleanAnd.leftNotBoolean 1 + arrayFilter.strict 3 + empty.notAllowed 2 + ternary.shortNotAllowed 1 + function.strict 1)
- Core PHPStan nullable-safety: 36 (property.nonObject 23 + method.nonObject 13)
- peststan: 7 (typeCoverage.paramTypeCoverage)
- Core PHPStan real type issues: 15 (argument.type 5 + return.type 3 + 7 singletons)

By area:
- tests: 85
- app: 52
- other (config/): 6

### Refines

- #18: factual premise corrected (0 violations was pre-strict-rules; policy stands).
- #17: policy refined — framework-idiom carve-outs exempt from retiring-ticket requirement.
- .1: acceptance criteria refined — types:check exits 0 requires the ignoreErrors block + .3 and .4 code fixes.
- .3: fix approach changed to assert guards.
close_reason: Resolved: keep strict-rules, one permanent framework-idiom carve-out (staticMethod.dynamicCall), fix all 82 remaining violations in code. Policy refined: framework-idiom carve-outs exempt from retiring-ticket requirement. See resolution notes.

title: Postgres extension management approach
description:
## Blocked by

- #40 — Select the PostgreSQL + pgvector + tsvector stack

---

## Question

How are PostgreSQL extensions (`pgvector` and any supplementary extensions) declared, installed, and verified across Herd (macOS arm64) and Linux CI — and does the SQLite Extension Manifest framework from decision #12 dissolve entirely or transform into a thinner Postgres equivalent?

## Context

**Supersedes** [#12](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/12) (SQLite extension bootstrap + diagnostics). **Material reason**: PostgreSQL loads extensions via `CREATE EXTENSION` against installed shared libraries; there is no per-connection load mechanism, no Native Extension Fault class, and no need for the Extension Connection Gate / Vector Capability Probe / Extension Sync Command / Offline Diagnostics / Health Report framework that #12 specified.

Decision [#11](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/11)'s Acceptance Stage 2 ("Native SQLite extension capability on Herd and CI") transforms into "Verify pgvector available on Herd + CI".

This ticket decides: extension declaration mechanism (migration-time `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS` vs post-install script); CI image choice (`ankane/pgvector` vs `pgvector/pgvector` official vs custom Dockerfile); Herd Pro Postgres capability verification; what (if any) `CONTEXT.md` SQLite-specific terms retire vs transform. Likely answer: most of the #12 framework dissolves; the residual concern is "is pgvector installed in the server?" which is `pg_extension` catalogue + `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS`.

## Out of scope

- The SQLite-specific framework (Extension Connection Gate, Native Extension Fault, etc.) — closed in [#21](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21), [#22](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/22).
- pgvector version pinning + tsvector config (separate ticket "Select the PostgreSQL + pgvector + tsvector stack").

title: Postgres schema design for the three sample products
description:
## Blocked by

- #40 — Select the PostgreSQL + pgvector + tsvector stack

---

## Question

How are the three product domains organized in PostgreSQL — separate `SCHEMAS` per product (`chinook`, `northwind`, `sakila`) vs product-prefixed tables in the `public` schema — and how does this interact with Laravel's schema builder, Eloquent model bindings, and `search_path` configuration?

## Context

**Partially supersedes** [#6](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/6) (which specified SQLite-conventional product-prefixed tables). The schema *shape* from #6 (UUIDv7 domain identities, `source_id` preservation, deterministic FK remapping, restricted relationships, typed Blob Assets) is database-agnostic and **stands**; only the PostgreSQL-specific organisation question is re-opened.

Decision [#5](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/5) requires each panel to own resources in a distinct namespace. PostgreSQL `SCHEMAS` offer a stronger isolation mechanism than table prefixes. Laravel supports Postgres schemas via `search_path` configuration and `Schema::connection(...)->create(...)`.

Decision [#7](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/7) (import + reset) operates per-product; schema-per-product aligns naturally with per-product reset semantics (drop + recreate schema is atomic).

This ticket decides: `SCHEMAS` vs prefix; Laravel/Eloquent integration pattern; `search_path` strategy (per-panel? global?); how the Source Identity Registry + Reset Run tables fit; how Federated Search across product schemas preserves product labels (T6.4).

## Out of scope

- Re-litigating #6's identity mapping (UUIDv7, `source_id`, FK remap) — DB-agnostic.
- Postgres stack selection (separate ticket).
- Search Projection design (#32, re-scoped).

title: Select the PostgreSQL + pgvector + tsvector stack
description:
## Question

What is the PostgreSQL-baseline stack for this application — Postgres major version pin, pgvector version pin, tsvector configuration (default language, dictionaries, ranking model), and the index strategy (HNSW vs ivfflat + parameters) for the active Embedding Profile's dimensionality?

## Context

**Supersedes** [#3](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/3) (sqlite-vec stack). **Material reason for re-opening**: T2.1 (#20) and T2.4 (#23) research revealed that Herd's stock PHP PDO build cannot load sqlite-vec. The deciding operator pivoted the DB tier to PostgreSQL 18 + pgvector (already running locally via Homebrew); see [resolution of #21](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21).

Decision [#8](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/8) (search tiers, embedding profile, RRF, transactional FTS) **stands** — only the underlying storage technology changes. pgvector's HNSW index is state-of-the-art; Postgres tsvector + GIN is more capable than FTS5.

Local environment (verified 2026-07-20):
- Postgres 18.0 (Homebrew `postgresql@18`) running with active worker processes
- `pgvector` installed via Homebrew
- `pdo_pgsql` + `pgsql` PHP extensions loaded in Herd's PHP
- Herd Pro includes managed PostgreSQL

This ticket decides: Postgres major pin (18.x), pgvector version pin, tsvector configuration (language(s), dictionaries, weights), HNSW vs ivfflat + index parameters for the Embedding Profile's dimensionality, and any supplementary extensions (e.g., `pg_trgm` for fuzzy, `unaccent` for diacritics).

## Out of scope

- Re-litigating the pivot itself (material reason recorded in #21's resolution).
- Schema organization (separate ticket "Postgres schema design for the three sample products").
- Embedding Profile provider/model (decision #8 stands — OpenAI pinned).
- Extension declaration mechanism (separate ticket "Postgres extension management approach").

title: Decide the Team Artefact schema and Team Owner policy boundary
description:
## Question

## Context

`CONTEXT.md`: *Team Artefact* is "a team-visible Saved Search or Dashboard owned by one team and attributed to its creator, even after that creator's membership ends. It does not alter shared sample data or restrict a Sample Product." *Team Owner* "has no authority over shared sample data." Decision [#9](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/9) separates "team-owned artefacts from global capabilities."

The Livewire teams starter ships Team, Membership, TeamOwner concept. This ticket integrates Team Artefact as a new domain concept owned by Team but attributed to User.

This ticket decides: Team Artefact table shape (Saved Search + Dashboard); attribution + ownership semantics; the Team Owner's policy over them; and how a Saved Search integrates with the Federated Search result page (T6.4).

## Out of scope

- Team-readable URLs / slug policy — out of scope per map #1.
- Portfolio Card layout — T7.1.

title: Decide the Search Projection virtual table design
description:
## Blocked by

- #40 — Select the PostgreSQL + pgvector + tsvector stack
- #41 — Postgres schema design for the three sample products

---

## Question

What is the PostgreSQL schema for the Search Projection — `tsvector` column + GIN index design, `vector(N)` column + HNSW index parameters, generated vs maintained `tsvector` (`GENERATED ALWAYS AS` STORED column vs trigger vs application-level), and how does transactional consistency between lexical and vector representations work under Postgres's transactional DDL?

## Context

**Re-scoped by the PostgreSQL pivot** — see [resolution of #21](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21). Original FTS5 + vec0 virtual table design replaced with PostgreSQL-native equivalents.

Decision [#8](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/8) required "transactional FTS with verified after-commit vectors." Under SQLite, FTS5 was transactional but vec0 required after-commit listener + verification. Under Postgres, **both tsvector and vector updates are transactional DDL/DML** — the after-commit workaround is no longer required.

`CONTEXT.md`'s *Search Projection* definition ("lexical representation is transactionally current; vector representation is derived after commit and independently verified") **needs revision**: under Postgres, both representations can be transactionally current. The embedding generation may still be asynchronous (queue job, T6.3), but that is a latency decision, not a transactional correctness requirement.

This ticket decides: `tsvector` column design (`GENERATED ALWAYS AS` + STORED vs trigger-updated vs application-maintained); GIN index parameters; `vector(N)` dimensionality from the Embedding Profile (T6.3); HNSW vs ivfflat + index parameters; whether to retain the after-commit verification step as defensive instrumentation or drop it as unnecessary.

## Out of scope

- The Postgres stack selection (ticket #40).
- Search Document content (T6.1, #31).
- Embedding Profile (T6.3, #33).
- Hybrid Retrieval / RRF (T6.4, #34).

title: Decide the Product Reset semantics
description:
## Question

What is the implementation shape of a Product Reset — how is the Reset Window marked (middleware flag, env signal, DB column), what is the atomic per-domain transactional scope, what does the Reset Evidence record contain (and exclude), and how does Reset Recovery retry?

## Context

`CONTEXT.md` defines *Product Reset*, *Reset Window*, *Reset Run*, *Reset Evidence*, *Baseline Invariant*, and *Reset Confirmation*. Decision [#7](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/7) requires "atomic per-product resets with stable identities, request-time edit cutoffs, hard publish gates." Decision [#11](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/11)'s *Reset Isolation Proof* mandates a success-and-fault-injection test that "restores only the target baseline while preserving Domain Identity."

This ticket decides: the Reset Window mechanism; the per-domain atomic transactional scope (where the Source Identity Registry lives during reset — T3.2); the Reset Evidence schema; the Reset Confirmation flow; and the recovery path on partial failure.

## Out of scope

- The Product Import pipeline — T4.1 (Reset is the inverse).
- Reset Isolation Proof test cases — those are T8.x acceptance gates.

comments.text:
# Decision: Spatie Permission, Shield, Fortify & Team co-existence boundary

_Resolved by grilling (HITL). Seven sub-decisions; shared understanding confirmed._

## 1. Partition principle — reframe, not consolidate
**Spatie is the sole capability/RBAC engine.** The starter's `TeamRole`/`TeamPermission` are **membership-position data** on `team_members` (like a `position` field), not a rival RBAC. **Spatie `teams` mode stays OFF** — verified against Spatie v7 docs: `teams` is a tenant-style permission-scoping axis (`setPermissionsTeamId()` per request), which contradicts CONTEXT.md's anti-tenant glossary. Full teams-mode consolidation rejected (~51 vs ~87 weighted: re-opens #16's "untouched starter" baseline, churns tested code under #17/#18 strict gates, redundant with the existing `belongsToMany` membership).

## 2. Role taxonomy
- `super_admin` = **System Operator** — Shield `Gate::before` bypass; subsumes all curator grants.
- `{product}_curator` (`chinook/northwind/sakila_curator`) = the per-product grants of the **singular** "Sample Curator" Global Capability.
- **Product Entitlement** = being authenticated (universal; never role-gated).

CONTEXT.md gains a refinement note: _Sample Curator is granted per Sample Product via the `{product}_curator` role; a user may hold it for one, some, or all products; System Operator (`super_admin`) implies all._

## 3. Filament ↔ Fortify coexistence — source-verified (Filament v5.1.1)
All four panels: `->authGuard('web')`, **omit** `->login()`/`->registration()`/`->passwordReset()`/`->emailVerification()`, **keep** `Authenticate::class`. Unauthenticated panel request → `Panel::getLoginUrl()` returns `null` (no login registered) → `Authenticate::redirectTo()` → framework `?? route('login')` → **Fortify `/login`** (no `RouteNotFoundException`). `canAccessPanel()` is the per-panel gate (#16 match pattern, docs-blessed). Fortify `LoginResponse` uses `redirect()->intended()` → bounce-back lands the user on their panel, free.

**#19's "inferred, not blessed" uncertainty → dissolved** at the source level. → 4-panel unauthenticated-redirect regression test added to #17.

## 4. Shield generation scope
`shield:generate --panel=admin` only. `TeamPolicy.php` untouched (Team is not a Filament Resource — managed by the starter's Livewire SFC per the anti-tenant stance). The glossary boundary ("Global Role Admin does not manage Team Ownership/membership/Product Entitlement") holds **by construction** — team-position is a pivot column, invisible to Shield; no UI guard needed. → product-policy-namespace arch rule added to #17.

## 5. Production operator onboarding
`php artisan operator:create` — env-driven (`OPERATOR_EMAIL`/`OPERATOR_PASSWORD`/`OPERATOR_NAME`), `firstOrCreate` User + personal team ("System Operator's Team") + `super_admin`, writes a **Supplementary Activity** audit row (#13), fails loud if creds unset, one-shot idempotent. **Dev-seeding moves from #16's baseline-operator migration to `DatabaseSeeder`** (migrations shouldn't mint identities from secrets — refines #16's mechanism, honors its intent). 2FA enrollment at first login (Fortify owns auth). Subsequent operators assigned via the RoleResource.

## 6. Team-context middleware — unchanged (benign coexistence recorded)
`SetTeamUrlDefaults` stays global but is **inert** for the four panel route trees (they declare no `{current_team}`/`{team}` param, so `URL::defaults` injects nothing). `EnsureTeamMembership` stays **route-scoped** to team routes (`{current_team}/dashboard`, membership/invitation flows) — structurally cannot gate a panel. Product Entitlement never team-gated.

## 7. Global Role Administration — runtime-managed under convention
Shield `RoleResource` **runtime-manages** (create + assign) global roles under the convention `super_admin` + one `{product}_curator` per Sample Product. Convention documented in CONTEXT.md, **not code-locked** — #16's dynamic `canAccessPanel` `{$panel->getId()}_curator` pattern is the enabler for future samples (adding a product just needs the role to exist). Safeguards live at the **code layer**: `super_admin` authority = role name + `Gate::before` (crisp regardless of runtime roles); Import/Reset CLI-gated on `hasRole('super_admin')` (#28/#29), **not** Shield permissions — runtime permission grants cannot escalate a curator to operator; team-position & Product Entitlement structurally unreachable. → #17 Authorization Matrix gains role×resource×panel cells, extended per new product role.

---

**Refines:** #9 (Global Capability realized), #13 (Admin-only Shield + Supplementary Activity), #16 (Q3 path verified; Q5 migration→seeder), #17 (3 new shapes: 4-panel redirect test, product-policy-namespace arch rule, Authorization Matrix role×resource×panel cells).
**Dissolves:** #19 (dual-role-system forks + "inferred, not blessed" coexistence).
**Unblocks:** #30 (Filament Resource generation — discovery roots + policy convention fixed), #36 (Team Artefact — Team Owner boundary fixed).
**Out of scope:** per-resource policy details (#30); production 2FA enrollment UX (Fortify); the actual Filament/Shield install (#16 execution).

title: Decide the Source Identity Registry survival-across-resets mechanism
description:
## Blocked by

- #24 — T3.1 Decide the UUIDv7 implementation strategy

---

## Question

How does the Source Identity Registry durably associate a Source Identity with its Domain Identity across independent Product Resets, given that the Product Reset discards the domain's local rows but must preserve identity continuity?

## Context

`CONTEXT.md` defines *Source Identity Registry* as "the durable association between a Source Identity and the matching Domain Identity across independent resets." *Product Reset* "discards that domain's local changes while preserving Domain Identities." So the registry must outlive the rows it tracks — either by living outside the reset transaction's scope, by being re-affirmed during import, or by being logically separate from the domain tables.

Decision [#6](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/6) specifies "preserve exact source identities, normalise values, restrict relationships and deletion." Decision [#7](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/7) specifies "stable identities" through the import/reset cycle.

This ticket decides: the registry's table location (per-domain vs a shared registry table), whether it lives inside or outside the reset transaction, and how it is (re)populated during Product Import.

## Out of scope

- The Product Import pipeline shape — T4.1.
- The Product Reset transactional strategy — T4.2.

description:

title: Decide the Extension Connection Gate implementation
description:
## Blocked by

- #20 — T2.1 Verify sqlite-vec v0.1.9 asset availability and digests (research)

---

## Question

What is the implementation shape of the Extension Connection Gate — which ServiceProvider boots it, where in the boot order it runs, what fail-closed behaviour it produces on a Native Extension Fault, and how it integrates with the app's SQLite connection configuration?

## Context

`CONTEXT.md` defines *Extension Connection Gate* as "the mandatory admission check for an eligible SQLite connection. A connection passes only when its approved native extension is available and its declared capability is demonstrably present." *Native Extension Fault* makes the application database unavailable until corrected. *Extension Fault Response* is "an intentionally minimal HTTP response… communicating unavailability and a Diagnostic Correlation without disclosing host or binary details." Decision [#12](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/12) pins the bootstrap and runtime diagnostics.

This ticket decides: the ServiceProvider class, its boot priority, the SQLite connection resolver hook, the fault response (HTTP 503 with Diagnostic Correlation), and the dispatch path that prevents DB access on fault.

## Out of scope

- The Vector Capability Probe SQL — T2.3.

title: Decide the Larastan target level and baseline policy
description:
## Question

What Larastan level is the target (level 6 / 8 / max with Larastan extensions), and is a baseline file allowed during the build (shrinking over time) or forbidden (forcing zero-violation commits)?

## Context

Larastan 3.9 is installed; `composer types:check` runs `phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M`. No `phpstan.neon` exists yet. Decision [#11](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/11)'s Acceptance Gate model implies a non-negotiable end state but does not specify the path.

A baseline supports incremental adoption through the build; zero-baseline forces per-commit discipline but may stall early scaffolding. Stage 1 scaffold work generates many model classes; strict typing from day 0 has cost/benefit trade-offs.

This ticket decides: target level; baseline policy (allowed-and-shrinking vs forbidden); where `phpstan.neon` lives; whether `level: max` is the terminal target even if a lower level gates PRs during the build.

## Out of scope

- Pint formatting rules (Pint is pre-configured; project overrides are separate).
- CI integration — that is T8.3.
close_reason: Resolved: lock level: max + no baseline, no ratchet. Empirical check showed the Livewire teams starter (app/ + bootstrap + config + database + routes/ + tests/) already passes PHPStan level: max with 0 violations and no baseline, with strict-rules + deprecation-rules + phpunit auto-loaded by extension-installer. Same strict-with-shrinking-carve-outs shape as #17: every ignoreErrors entry MUST cite a bd/GitHub execution ticket that retires it; orphan ignores flagged by a sibling arch test. Execution follow-up filed as bd …eac5a270.1 (single-file phpstan.neon edit). Closes the loop opened in #17's 'Precedent set' footnote.

title: Decide the test pyramid: layers, coverage target, and arch rules
description:
## Question

What is the test pyramid for this application — which layers (Unit, Feature, Architecture, Browser/Dusk) are mandatory vs aspirational, what coverage target applies per layer and overall, and what `arch()` boundary rules does Pest enforce?

## Context

description:
## Destination

Implement all twelve decisions from [map #1](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/1) to production-ready completion — a Laravel 13 + PHP 8.5 application presenting Chinook, Northwind, and Sakila as three sample products within one application, with an Admin Filament 5 panel plus one Filament 5 panel per product, hybrid search via FTS5 + sqlite-vec v0.1.9, Spatie Permission + Shield authorization, reproducible Product Import and independent Product Reset, and the version-controlled Implementation-Readiness Dossier — passing the Two-Environment Operational Gate (Linux x86_64 CI green on every PR; Herd macOS arm64 CLI + HTTP evidence on each release candidate), Larastan at the target level, comprehensive Pest coverage, and proportional documentation per the software documentation lifecycle.

## Notes

- **Source of plan:** [map #1](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/1) and its twelve child decisions ([#2](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/2)–[#13](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/13)). [Issue #11](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/11) defines the eight Acceptance Stages and six mandatory evidence types — they are the spine of this map.
- **Domain glossary:** [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/blob/main/CONTEXT.md) — especially *Acceptance Gate*, *Acceptance Stage*, *Acceptance Evidence*, *Baseline Evidence Fixture*, *Reset Isolation Proof*, *Authorization Acceptance Matrix*, *Golden Search Corpus*, *Two-Environment Operational Gate*, *Implementation-Readiness Dossier*.
- **Plan-only mode:** each ticket resolves ONE decision; execution is handed off once the way is clear. No ticket carries implementation into itself.
- **Skills every session should consult:** `wayfinder`, `laravel-best-practices`, `pest-testing`, `livewire-development`, `fluxui-development`, `fortify-development`, `tailwindcss-development`; plus `domain-modeling` / `grilling` / `prototype` / `research` as the ticket type dictates.
- **Verify version-sensitive claims** against official Laravel 13, Livewire 4, Filament 5, sqlite-vec v0.1.9, and upstream sample-dataset sources. Issues #2, #3, #4 pinned these — do not re-litigate without a recorded reason.
- **DATABASE TIER (pivot recorded 2026-07-20):** the application uses **PostgreSQL 18 + pgvector + tsvector** — not SQLite. Resolving #21 revealed Herd's stock PHP PDO build cannot load sqlite-vec (T2.1/T2.4 findings), and the operator pivoted the entire DB tier to PostgreSQL, which is already running locally. This re-opens decisions #3 (sqlite-vec → pgvector), partially #6 (schema dialect), and #12 (SQLite extension bootstrap → Postgres extension management). New tickets: [#40](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/40) (stack), [#41](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/41) (schema), [#42](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/42) (extensions). Closed as out of scope: [#21](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21) (T2.2 Extension Connection Gate), [#22](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/22) (T2.3 Vector Capability Probe). Decisions #2, #4, #5, #7, #8, #9, #10, #13 unchanged.
- **Each ticket sized to one 100K-token agent session;** claim by assigning to the driver before any work.
- **Repo state at chart time:** bootstrapped (Laravel 13.17, PHP 8.5, Livewire teams starter with Fortify + Flux 2 + passkeys + 2FA + teams, Pest 4, Larastan 3, Pint, Boost, pnpm/Vite, `tests.yml` workflow, composer scripts for `lint` / `lint:check` / `types:check` / `test` / `ci:check`). **Not yet installed:** Filament 5, Spatie Permission/Shield. **Database tier (pivot, stack selected via #40):** Herd-managed PostgreSQL 18.x + pgvector 0.8.x + pg_trgm + unaccent on `127.0.0.1:5437` (service name `Herd_PostgreSQL`, DB `laravel`, user `root`); `pdo_pgsql` loaded in Herd's PHP. No domain code yet.

## Decisions so far

- [Pivot to PostgreSQL + pgvector](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21) — Resolving [#21 (T2.2 Extension Connection Gate)](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/21) revealed (via T2.1 / T2.4 research) that Herd's stock PHP PDO build cannot load sqlite-vec. The operator pivoted the entire DB tier to PostgreSQL 18 + pgvector (already running locally). Dissolves the Extension Connection Gate / Native Extension Fault / SQLite Extension Manifest / Vector Capability Probe concepts. Re-opens decisions #3, #6, #12 via three new tickets: [#40](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/40) (stack), [#41](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/41) (schema), [#42](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/42) (extensions). [#22 (T2.3)](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/22) closed in parallel.
- [PostgreSQL + pgvector + tsvector stack selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/40) — Herd-managed PG 18.x + pgvector 0.8.x (Herd-bundled; patch-drift follows Herd's release cadence). HNSW index with pgvector defaults (`m=16`, `ef_construction=64`, query-time `ef_search=40`) for the 1,536-dim `text-embedding-3-small` profile from #8. tsvector config: `english` + `unaccent` via custom `en_unaccent` text search configuration; `ts_rank_cd` ranking with ABCD field weights (D=title/name, C=description, B=category, A=identifier). Extensions: `vector`, `unaccent`, `pg_trgm`. Herd Postgres on :5437 was WAL-corrupted at grilling start (`PANIC: could not locate a valid checkpoint record`); re-initialized losslessly via `herd services:delete` + `herd services:create`. pgvector 0.8.1 currently bundled; upstream stable is 0.8.5 (gap noted, not blocking under Herd-bundled pin policy). Supersedes #3; unblocks #41 and #42.
- [Postgres schema design selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/41) — Three product schemas (`chinook`, `northwind`, `sakila`) + `public` for Core Application and shared infrastructure; single physical database, per-product schemas (not separate DBs). Product tables drop the prefix — partial supersession of #6 (`chinook.artists` not `chinook_artists`); all other #6 shape decisions stand. Single `pgsql` connection with `search_path=public`; every product-table reference schema-qualified in migrations and Eloquent (`#[Table('chinook.artists')]`). Rationale: same-named tables across product schemas (`customers` ×3, `employees` ×2, `categories` ×2) make a global multi-schema `search_path` impossible. Search Projections per-product (`chinook.search_projections`, etc.); drops atomically with `DROP SCHEMA … CASCADE` during Product Reset — aligns with #7 atomic-per-product. Source Identity Registry, Reset Run, Pin Manifest, and the shared `en_unaccent` text search config live in `public` so they survive per-product reset. Federated Search uses `UNION ALL` across the three product schemas with literal `product_tenant` labels. Migrations organised per-product (`database/migrations/{chinook,northwind,sakila}/`). #7's stale "SQLite single-writer" Reset Window rationale retired (Postgres is MVCC); Reset Window behaviour unchanged. Unblocks #32 (column shape) and #42 (extension lifecycle).
- [Postgres extension management selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/42) — Single early migration `0001_01_01_000000_create_postgres_extensions.php` declares `vector`, `unaccent`, `pg_trgm` extensions + `en_unaccent` text search config via `DB::statement('CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS …')` on the default `pgsql` connection. `down()` is a no-op (extensions are infrastructure; rolling back must not cascade-drop data). No version pin in DDL (Herd-bundled policy from #40). No `pgsql::direct` for now (default connection sufficient for Herd + CI; swappable if pooler enters). CI: `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` Docker service container. Verification: Pest test `test_postgres_extensions_are_installed` (gates every CI build), `php artisan pgsql:check` command (deploy-time operator check), README docs (Herd Pro prerequisite). All 14 SQLite-specific terms from #12 fully dissolve; none transform. Supersedes #12; closes the Postgres-pivot trio (#40+#41+#42). DB tier is now fully charted for execution.
- [Search Projection column shape selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/32) — Per-product `*.search_projections` table: UUIDv7 Domain Identity as PK directly (integer `search_id` bridge from #8 dissolves — pgvector has no integer-PK requirement); four weight-class text columns (`weight_d/c/b/a_text`) written by Postgres trigger from the source entity's Search Document fields (#31 owns the per-entity mapping); `document_tsv tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (setweight(to_tsvector('en_unaccent', …), 'D') || …) STORED` materialises #40's ABCD weighting in-storage (PG18 canonical pattern, transactionally current by construction); `embedding vector(1536)` + `embedding_profile` + `content_digest` + `embedded_at` + `embedding_state` (`pending`/`complete`/`failed`/`mismatched`/`lexical_only`) for the semantic side; tier-2 rows live in the same table with NULL embedding (`lexical_only` state, HNSW skips them automatically). Integrity: Postgres trigger (authoritative content writer + state reset) + Eloquent observer (queues embedding job post-commit). After-commit verification transforms — drops defensive re-check (ACID covers it), adds Baseline Invariant `embedding_state NOT IN ('complete','lexical_only')` count = 0 at end of Product Import/Reset. HNSW (`m=16`, `ef_construction=64`, `ef_search=40`) + GIN (`fastupdate=on`) defaults confirmed. Refines #8 (search_id retires, after-commit rationale becomes operational not correctness), #41 (concrete shape for the per-product projection tables), #7 (new publish-gate Baseline Invariant). Unblocks #33 (Embedding Profile impl — target columns fixed) and #34 (RRF + Federated Search — query targets fixed).
- [Search Document shape per entity selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/31) — Tier assignments: 11 tier-1 (hybrid — Chinook Artist/Album/Track/Playlist, Northwind Product/Category/Supplier, Sakila Film/Actor/Category/Language), 13 tier-2 (lexical-only — Chinook Customer/Employee/Invoice/Genre, Northwind Customer/Employee/Order/Shipper, Sakila Customer/Staff/Rental/Payment/Store; operator override placed Staff/Payment/Store as tier 2 despite auth-credential and money-sensitivity concerns), ~16 tier-3 (excluded — all join tables, contact/location tables, internal-org tables, `film_text`, `media_types`). Tier-1 field→weight mapping pinned per entity per #40's ABCD scheme: weight_d = title/name, weight_c = description (Track.Composer, Product.QuantityPerUnit, Film.Description, Category.Description), weight_b = category (Track→Genre.Name via FK subquery, Product→Category.CategoryName via FK subquery, Film→Category.name via film_category join + Rating), weight_a = `source_id` (universal). FK→Name resolution via subquery inside the PL/pgSQL trigger function (no denormalised columns on source tables). Search Surface exclusives consolidated: contact data, location data, money (`*_minor`), Blob Assets, auth credentials (`Staff.username`/`password`), relationship-only rows, internal metadata, pre-computed search columns. `entity_type` discriminator = singular snake_case (Eloquent morph type convention); product identity carried by schema name per #41 (federated query adds literal `product_tenant` label). Produces the complete CASE mapping table for #32's trigger execution. Closes the wayfinder-level search cluster — #33/#34 are implementation tickets, no further wayfinder decisions required.
- [Upstream datasets re-verified — zero drift](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/27) — All three sources (Chinook `lerocha/chinook-database` @ `7f67772`, Northwind `jpwhite3/northwind-SQLite3` @ `4f56e7f`, Sakila `bradleygrant/sakila-sqlite3` @ `9394b42`) re-verified 2026-07-21 against live sources with freshly recomputed SHA-256 digests; every pinned commit is still HEAD of its default branch, every digest matches #4 byte-for-byte, no mirror moved or archived. One non-material note for #28: Chinook's `v1.4.5` *tag* is not byte-equivalent to the pinned commit (CRLF→LF normalization) — importer must resolve by commit SHA, never by tag. Pin Manifest still lives only in the #4 audit doc; materialising it into the repo is #28/T4.1's job. Unblocks #28 (Product Import pipeline).
- [Filament 5 + Livewire teams starter co-install verified](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/19) — Co-install is viable on the shared `web` guard; Shield v4 carries the Filament 5 compatibility badge. No guard collision, no route collision (Fortify `/login` and Filament `/admin/login` are in disjoint URI trees). Four decision forks surfaced — these are the spine of #16 and #26: (1) **2FA ownership** — Fortify's `TwoFactorAuthenticatable` vs Filament v5's built-in MFA, one must own the challenge flow; (2) **panel scope + tenancy** — `/admin` as global cross-team panel vs Filament tenancy with `Team` as tenant (the starter's `EnsureTeamMembership` reads a `{current_team}` route param panel routes don't carry, so it cannot gate `/admin` as-is); (3) **dual role systems** — Shield's global spatie roles vs the starter's team-scoped `TeamRole`/`TeamPermission` enums, need an explicit mapping policy; (4) **policy-directory convention** — Shield writes to `app/Policies/` and would target the existing `TeamPolicy` if a `TeamResource` is added. One open uncertainty flagged for #26: no official Filament v5 + Fortify coexistence recipe exists — the "reuse Fortify session, disable Filament auth" path is inferred from guest-access docs, not blessed. Unblocks #16 and #26.
- [UUIDv7 implementation strategy selected](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/24) — Laravel 13's native `HasUuids` trait generates UUIDv7 by default (verified against 13.x Eloquent docs; `ramsey/uuid` 4.9.3 + `symfony/uid` 8.1.0 already present). No package, no custom generator, no `newUniqueId()` override. **Six decisions:** (1) **native generation + registry reuse** over deterministic derivation — #25's existence implies it is the identity-continuity mechanism (content-hash derivation would make the registry redundant and forfeit v7 index locality); (2) **Postgres native `uuid` column** (`$table->uuid('id')`, no `AsBinary` cast — that's for DBs lacking native uuid); (3) **rewrite the starter migrations in place** (`users` + `teams` + join tables: `id()`→`uuid('id')`, `foreignId()`→`foreignUuid()`) — pre-data, `0001_01_01_…` designed to be edited, repo bootstrapped *from* not forked *of* the starter; (4) **per-model `use HasUuids;`** — trait sets `$incrementing`/`$keyType` internally so it's one line per model, consistent with #41's per-model `#[Table]` attribute, no shared base class (YAGNI); (5) **UUIDv7 PK on every app-owned table** — `users`, `teams`, `team_members`, `team_invitations` (operator override — moved in for consistency: no bigInteger PKs anywhere in app-owned tables), all product-domain tables, shared `public` domain tables; framework-standard keys kept only on pure Laravel infra (`password_reset_tokens`, `sessions`, `jobs`, `failed_jobs`, `job_batches`, `cache`, `cache_locks`, `migrations`); (6) **import hook = explicit-id-on-reuse** — importer sets `$model->id` from the registry on a hit (bypassing `HasUuids`), leaves it unset on a miss so the trait generates, then records the mapping. Overriding `newUniqueId()` rejected (couples models to registry, needs source-context only the importer has). Unblocks #25 (registry shape now the only open identity question) and #28 (with #27).

Pest test `test_postgres_extensions_are_installed` gates the merge. The stage itself stays; gate content is now **fully specified** after #40 + #41 + #42.

title: Wayfinder — Laravel Sample Database Products
description:
## Destination

Produce an implementation-ready, decision-complete plan for a Laravel 13 application that presents Chinook, Northwind, and Sakila as three sample products within one application, with an Admin Filament 5 panel, one Filament panel per product, reproducible customised data, and text plus vector search.

## Notes

- Scaffold target: `/Users/s-a-c/Herd/samples-20260717`; PHP 8.5+ and Laravel 13 with the Livewire teams starter, Pest, pnpm, Boost, development dependencies, Git, and GitHub.
- Filament 5: one Admin panel plus Chinook, Northwind, and Sakila panels. Every panel owns resources in a distinct subfolder/namespace.
- Custom application UI uses Livewire single-file components. Native Filament resources, forms, tables, and pages are the explicit exception.
- Use one physical SQLite database. Prefix sample tables by domain; keep framework/core names conventional. Cross-domain joins belong in explicit reporting/search read models.
- UUIDv7 primary keys cover users, teams, and all sample-domain entities. Laravel infrastructure tables keep framework-standard keys.
- Preserve each upstream entity's original identifier in an indexed `source_id` and deterministically remap foreign keys.
- Sample datasets are globally shared, editable, and independently resettable to pinned upstream baselines. Teams own access and user-generated artefacts, not cloned datasets.
- Provide both per-sample and federated text/vector search; results retain product identity and link to their owning panel/resource.
- Every session should use `wayfinder`, `laravel-best-practices`, and the relevant domain/research skills. Verify version-sensitive claims against official Laravel, Livewire, Filament, SQLite, extension, and upstream repository sources.
- Apply the software documentation lifecycle proportionately: evidence, product scope, requirements, traceability, solution design, delivery, and assurance.

## Decisions so far

- [Verify Laravel 13, Livewire SFC, and Filament 5 integration boundaries](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/2) — Require PHP 8.5+, use the Livewire teams starter, then Filament 5 with four isolated discovery roots; custom UI is native Livewire SFC and Filament UI stays native.
- [Select the SQLite text and vector extension stack](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/3) — Use built-in FTS5 plus pinned sqlite-vec v0.1.9 on the PHP 8.5+ baseline, backed by an integer search projection that maps to UUIDv7 domain records.
- [Audit and pin the three upstream sample datasets](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/4) — Import immutable, checksum-verified upstream artifacts into Laravel-owned schemas and preserve scalar/composite source identities through explicit remapping.
- [Define the application, domain, panel, and resource namespace architecture](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/5) — Put samples in separate App\Domain modules, keep shared core in App\Models and App\Search, give every panel an exclusive App\Filament root, and scope custom Livewire SFCs by product.
- [Define the transformed schemas and UUIDv7 identity mapping](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/6) — Use Laravel-conventional product-prefixed tables and stable UUIDv7 domain identities; preserve exact source identities, normalise values, restrict relationships and deletion, and keep BLOB assets typed.
- [Define deterministic import and independent reset semantics](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/7) — Use one verified Product Import pipeline and atomic per-product resets with stable identities, request-time edit cutoffs, hard publish gates, and compact evidence.
- [Define hybrid search, embeddings, and index synchronisation](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/8) — Use three search tiers, a pinned OpenAI embedding profile, RRF-ranked product-owned results, and transactional FTS with verified after-commit vectors.
- [Define team authorization and product entitlement semantics](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/9) — Keep Sample Product access universal, separate team-owned artefacts from global capabilities, and protect product resets with explicit System Operator confirmation.
- [Define cross-product reporting and overall-panel read models](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/10) — Make Admin a product portfolio of product-scoped snapshot/query cards, with no cross-product business comparison or warehouse.
- [Define verification, delivery, and operational acceptance](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/11) — Require staged, traceable gates for baselines, resets, authorization, search, supported runtimes, and an implementation-readiness dossier.
- [Define native SQLite extension bootstrap and runtime diagnostics](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/12) — Pin and verify sqlite-vec assets, gate every SQLite connection, fail closed with private diagnostics, and prove the native matrix in Herd and CI.
- [Define the authorization, audit, and configurable-dashboard package boundary](https://github.com/s-a-c/samples-20260717/issues/13) — Use Spatie Permission with Admin-only Shield, selected supplementary activity, and code-owned cards; defer presentation and generic-form extensions.

## Not yet specified

- None.

## Out of scope

- Customer-facing music commerce or an attempt to merge the three sample domains into one shared business domain.
- A later product-facing or shareable Team Artefact experience—including human-readable URLs and a slug policy—is deferred to a separate future destination; no current route or sluggable package is selected.
- Separate physical database files or per-team clones of the sample datasets.
- Production hosting topology beyond the local Herd target and reference CI portability.
- Implementing the destination while this planning map is being charted.
- A separate data warehousing/OLAP enhancement for analytical cross-product comparison; it is a possible future destination, not part of this one-database application plan.
